answer: Randomized Registration Inlet. Each period, agents derive a seed from a public comet beacon and hash it with their identity key to get a slot in a fixed-size inlet. Only agents whose slot falls below a threshold quota are admitted that round. An attacker cannot precompute favorable slots because the beacon value is unknown until broadcast, so mass-registering identities yields no advantage. Registering N identities costs N full registrations plus wasted slots, and each admitted identity must survive a random glacier audit that reveals its key history.
